Psychiatry Billing Services

Billing for Psychiatrists Is Not
the Same as Billing for Therapists

Psychiatry sits between medicine and therapy, and the claim has to reflect both.

A psychiatrist or psychiatric NP often does two jobs in one visit: manages medication and delivers psychotherapy. The claim therefore carries an E/M code and a time-based psychotherapy add-on, and each has its own documentation rules. Therapy-only billing companies tend to code the visit as one or the other, which leaves money on the table or creates audit exposure.

Psychiatry also has procedure lines that general billers rarely see: transcranial magnetic stimulation, electroconvulsive therapy, esketamine administration with required observation, and long-acting injectable visits. Each has payer-specific prior authorization and supply or drug billing requirements.

PMEx codes from the note in your EHR, submits within 24 hours of the signed visit, and works every denial. You keep your EHR. We work inside it.

THE EDUCATION

What Makes Psychiatry Billing Easy to Get Wrong

Psychiatry pairs a medical E/M visit with time-based psychotherapy, interactive complexity, and procedure-level coding that general billers rarely see, and a small coding gap becomes a recurring denial pattern.

The core psychiatry claim is an E/M code plus a psychotherapy add-on: 99202 to 99205 for new patients or 99212 to 99215 for established patients, with 90833, 90836 or 90838 for 16 to 37, 38 to 52, and 53 or more minutes of psychotherapy. The psychotherapy time must be documented separately from the E/M work, and the E/M level is selected on medical decision making rather than on total time when an add-on is billed.

Interactive complexity (90785) can be reported with the add-on codes and with 90791 and 90792 when specific complicating factors are documented, but it cannot be billed with an E/M alone. Practices that miss it lose reimbursement on every qualifying visit, and practices that overuse it invite review.

Initial evaluations are split between 90791 (psychiatric diagnostic evaluation without medical services) and 90792 (with medical services). Choosing wrong is a common reason for downcoding and for audit findings.

Add telehealth modifiers and place of service rules, behavioral health carve-out plans such as Optum and Carelon (formerly Beacon), and mental health parity limits, and a small coding gap becomes a recurring denial pattern.

CODE 01 E/M + Add-On

The standard psychiatry visit pairs an E/M level with 90833, 90836 or 90838 when psychotherapy is delivered and documented.

CODE 02 90791 vs
90792

Diagnostic evaluation without or with medical services. The right code depends on what the prescriber actually documents.

CODE 03 Prior Auth

TMS, esketamine, ECT and psychological testing commonly require authorization before the first session.

CODE 04 Parity

Behavioral health plans may not impose stricter limits than medical benefits under MHPAEA. We track and challenge violations.

The most common psychiatry revenue leak:

Visits billed as an E/M alone when psychotherapy was delivered and documented. A properly supported 90833 add-on is paid on top of the E/M. PMEX reviews your notes for qualifying psychotherapy time and applies the add-on only when the documentation supports it.

Where Psychiatry Practices Lose Revenue

Three coding gaps that quietly cost psychiatry practices every month

Most psychiatry revenue loss does not come from visible denials. It comes from claims that are paid at a lower level than the visit supported, or not billed at all because the add-on, the evaluation level or the procedure line was never captured.

PMEX audits your recent visits against your notes and shows you exactly where the gaps are.

Add-On Capture

Psychotherapy time that never reaches the claim

When psychotherapy is delivered and separately timed in the note, 90833, 90836 or 90838 can be billed with the E/M. PMEX staff flag qualifying visits and confirm the documentation before billing.

Prior Auth Gaps

Treatment courses without an active authorization

TMS, esketamine and testing often require approval for a defined number of sessions. PMEX staff track the count and the expiry so renewals go in before the limit.

Carve-Out Routing

Claims sent to the wrong behavioral health entity

Optum, Carelon Behavioral Health and similar managed behavioral health organizations are identified at eligibility so the claim goes to the right place the first time.

Common Questions

Psychiatry billing answered

Can a psychiatrist bill an E/M and psychotherapy on the same day?
Yes, when the psychotherapy is a separately identifiable service. The visit is billed as an E/M plus a psychotherapy add-on (90833, 90836 or 90838), the psychotherapy time must be documented separately from the E/M work, and the E/M level is selected on medical decision making.
What is the difference between 90791 and 90792?
90791 is a psychiatric diagnostic evaluation without medical services. 90792 includes medical services such as a physical assessment or prescribing decisions. The correct code depends on what is documented in the visit.
When can interactive complexity 90785 be billed?
It can be reported with 90791, 90792, and the psychotherapy add-on codes when documented complicating factors are present, such as a third party who must be involved or a communication barrier. It cannot be billed with an E/M alone.
Does PMEX bill TMS and esketamine?
Yes. We handle TMS codes 90867, 90868 and 90869, ECT 90870, and esketamine G2082 and G2083, including prior authorization tracking and the observation documentation payers expect.
How do you handle telepsychiatry claims?
We map modifier 95, POS 02 or POS 10, and audio-only rules to each payer and state before the claim is submitted, and we track changes to Medicare telehealth rules as they occur.
Can you bill for psychiatric NPs?
Yes. We bill psychiatric NPs and PAs under their own NPI where allowed and under supervising physician rules where required, following the payer and state rules that apply.
What is a behavioral health carve-out?
Some health plans route mental health benefits to a separate managed behavioral health organization such as Optum or Carelon. Claims sent to the medical plan are denied, so we identify the correct entity at eligibility.
Which EHRs do you work with?
We work inside your existing EHR, including Valant, Luminello, SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, Tebra, DrChrono, Athenahealth, Epic, eClinicalWorks and Elation, among others.
Do you handle credentialing for new prescribers?
Yes. We enroll new psychiatrists and psychiatric NPs with Medicare, Medicaid and commercial plans, including behavioral health carve-out entities.
How fast are claims submitted?
Claims are submitted within 24 hours of the signed note once the documentation supports the codes.
What does psychiatry billing cost with PMEX?
Pricing starts at 2.49% of monthly collections, with fixed plans from $450 per month. Contact PMEX for a quote based on your provider count and visit volume.
How do I get started?
Request a free audit. We review a sample of your recent visits and remittances and show you where revenue is being missed before you commit to anything.
